subject.title: fix: reconcile timed-out gateway message actions

question: Should timed-out message-action reconciliation guarantee duplicate prevention only while the current Gateway process survives, or must it also survive a Gateway restart?
rationale: Current main supplies only an in-memory in-flight join and five-minute process-local result cache; restart-safe reconciliation requires a materially different persisted operation or receipt contract.

options.title: Accept bounded reconciliation
options.body: Merge after real seam and channel proof, with restart during the ambiguous window explicitly outside the guarantee.

options.title: Require restart-safe identity
options.body: Persist operation or delivery-receipt identity before merging so a restarted Gateway can reconcile the original action.

options.title: Pause this retry design
options.body: Defer or close the PR if neither bounded nor persisted reconciliation is an acceptable product contract.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded reconciliation
recommendation.body: Merge after real seam and channel proof, with restart during the ambiguous window explicitly outside the guarantee.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current message-action protocol and outbound timeout policy, making him the strongest available owner for the guarantee boundary.
